name: Four Seasons Resort Seychelles at Desroches Island
insider_take: This is Robinson Crusoe luxury at its finest – a pristine coral island where you're more likely to encounter giant tortoises than other tourists.
whats_special: Desroches Island spans just 3.7 square miles and sits atop an ancient coral atoll 150 miles southwest of Mahé. The resort occupies the entire island, meaning you'll have 14 kilometers of powder-white beaches virtually to yourself. The island is also a sanctuary for over 100 Aldabra giant tortoises that roam freely across the property – some weighing up to 550 pounds and over 100 years old.
pro_tip: Book the sunrise fishing excursion – Desroches sits on the edge of a 4,000-foot drop-off where yellowfin tuna, wahoo, and marlin are abundant. The resort's fleet includes a 38-foot game fishing boat with expert local guides.
dont_miss: The island's airstrip doubles as a nesting ground for sooty terns between May and October, creating one of nature's most spectacular wildlife displays. Also explore the ruins of the old coconut plantation and copra factory from the early 1900s, scattered throughout the island's interior jungle paths.
pros: Exclusive private island setting surrounded by pristine coral reefs and turquoise Indian Ocean waters
Spacious, elegantly appointed villas with private pools and direct beach or lagoon access
World-class diving, snorkeling, and water sports amid one of the Indian Ocean's most biodiverse marine ecosystems
Exceptional Four Seasons service with highly personalized attention and bespoke island experiences
Outstanding dining featuring fresh, locally sourced seafood and international cuisine in stunning open-air settings
cons: Remote island location requires a charter flight from Mahé, adding travel time and cost
Ultra-luxury pricing places this resort among the most expensive destinations in the Indian Ocean
Limited off-resort options due to the island's secluded, self-contained nature
